claude.sample_unit: benchmark clinical research questions (400 model-configuration runs); plus 617 BiomixQA questions

links.outcome: Accuracy/score with vs without knowledge-graph grounding of LLM outputs
links.effect: GPT-5.5 mean score 1.05 to 1.27 (OR 1.78, p=0.0029); Claude Opus 4.8 0.84 to 1.02 (OR 1.50, p=0.013); BiomixQA MCQ accuracy rose 0.752 to 0.902 (GPT-5.5) and 0.807 to 0.876 (Opus); TF unchanged.
links.quote: For GPT-5.5, the mean score increased from 1.05 without the knowledge graph to 1.27 with it (ordinal OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.22–2.61, p = 0.0029); for Claude Opus 4.8, it increased from 0.84 to 1.02 (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.09–2.05, p = 0.013).

links.outcome: Expert-graded correctness of agentic LLM answers on 100 clinical research tasks
links.effect: Mean scores were only about 1.0–1.3 out of 2; submaximal runs reflected temporal logic, denominator and mapping errors; scores were lower with KG for 22 GPT-5.5 and 15 Claude questions.
links.quote: Scores were lower with knowledge graph access for 22 GPT-5.5 and 15 Claude Opus 4.8 questions; recurrent causes remained specific query-construction and ontology-handling errors rather than a general limitation of knowledge graph integration (see Supplementary Data 1).

unlisted_practices: Read-only enforcement of agent database access at prompt, connector, and database-account layers
Logging and exposing all generated SQL/Cipher queries for expert audit
Model Context Protocol tool interface connecting LLMs to EHR and knowledge graph
Standardized replication protocol for real-world studies under expert supervision

links.outcome: biomedical MCQ accuracy with SPOKE grounding
links.effect: MCQ accuracy rose 0.807→0.876 for Opus and 0.752→0.902 for GPT-5.5; errors reduced 35.6% and 60.5%.
links.quote: Multiple-choice accuracy rose from 0.807 (95% CI 0.759–0.847) to 0.876 (0.834–0.908) for Opus 4.8, a paired gain of +6.9 percentage points (McNemar p = 0.0055), and from 0.752 (0.700–0.797) to 0.902 (0.863–0.930) for GPT-5.5, +15.0 points ( p < 0.001), equivalent to a 35.6% and a 60.5% reduction in errors, respectively ( Figure 2D ).

links.effect: Scores were lower with KG access for 22 GPT-5.5 and 15 Claude Opus 4.8 questions due to such errors.
links.quote: Scores were lower with knowledge graph access for 22 GPT-5.5 and 15 Claude Opus 4.8 questions; recurrent causes remained specific query-construction and ontology-handling errors rather than a general limitation of knowledge graph integration (see Supplementary Data 1).

links.effect: OMOP standardization may incompletely capture specialty panels or local codes, reducing event counts and statistical power.
links.quote: This attenuation likely reflects differences in data architecture between the Clinical Data Warehouse used in the original study—which provided direct access to all laboratory values—and the OMOP data model used in our replication, where laboratory results undergo vocabulary standardization that may incompletely capture specialty panels or non-standard local codes, reducing both event counts and statistical power.

unlisted_practices: Model Context Protocol agent connecting an OMOP EHR and biomedical knowledge graph for real-world evidence generation
Standardized LLM-assisted protocol for replicating published observational studies

links.effect: Multiple-choice accuracy rose from 0.807 to 0.876 for Opus 4.8 (p=0.0055) and from 0.752 to 0.902 for GPT-5.5 (p<0.001); true/false accuracy did not change.
